subject.title: [Feature]: Add optional capability descriptors to tool definitions

question: What canonical tool capability taxonomy and trust semantics should OpenClaw expose to plugin policy and audit consumers?
rationale: The requested descriptors become public Plugin SDK/Gateway security-policy inputs and overlap action provenance, default-deny capabilities, plugin egress intent, and Security Matrix work, so automation should not choose the permanent security contract.

options.title: Define unified descriptor contract
options.body: Add a single additive tool behavior descriptor model with documented unknown/advisory semantics and projection through SDK, Gateway catalog/effective inventory, before_tool_call, trusted policy, docs, and tests.

options.title: Fold into default-deny capability model
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader capability permission system so descriptor fields are designed only with the eventual authorization model.

options.title: Limit to Security Matrix for now
options.body: Keep descriptors internal to the observe-only Security Matrix/audit path until maintainers are ready to expose a public plugin/Gateway contract.

recommendation.title: Define unified descriptor contract
recommendation.body: Add a single additive tool behavior descriptor model with documented unknown/advisory semantics and projection through SDK, Gateway catalog/effective inventory, before_tool_call, trusted policy, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the adjacent host-hook foundation and are the clearest owner for a public plugin SDK contract decision.
